citation: Yuan et al. (2024), Whispers that Shake Foundations: Analyzing and Mitigating False Premise Hallucinations in Large Language Models
demonstrated_mechanism: Builds false-premise datasets through triple selection, corruption, and templated question construction; identifies false-premise attention heads and mitigates them with FAITH by constraining about 1% of heads, with controlled accuracy experiments.
inference_only_transfer: The mechanism is model-internal attention intervention, not source-grounded argument extraction, provenance, context compression, or scholastic-form control; applicability to project prompts is inferential.
novelty_overlap_or_threat: Threatens weak evaluation claims around false-premise/assumption handling and provides a concrete adversarial dataset-construction protocol; does not threaten the full context-engineering composition.
missing_boundaries: No argument-span extraction, objection/reply representation, proof dependency preservation, citation audit, or compact-context objective; datasets are factual triples and templates rather than historical arguments.
hostile_countertest: If false-premise terminology and reported gains are ignored, the triple-corruption controls and head-level intervention remain real. The paper therefore survives as an evaluation/robustness comparator, not a pipeline duplicate.
